extraction.name: Microsoft Common Objects in COntext (MS COCO)
extraction.description: A large-scale dataset for object recognition, contextual reasoning, and precise 2D localization in scene understanding. It contains 2.5 million labeled instances of 91 common object categories across 328,000 images of complex everyday scenes.
extraction.creator: Tsung-Yi Lin; Michael Maire; Serge Belongie; Lubomir Bourdev; Ross Girshick; James Hays; Pietro Perona; Deva Ramanan; C. Lawrence Zitnick; Piotr Dollár
extraction.citeAs: Tsung-Yi Lin, Michael Maire, Serge Belongie, Lubomir Bourdev, Ross Girshick, James Hays, Pietro Perona, Deva Ramanan, C. Lawrence Zitnick, Piotr Dollár. Microsoft COCO: Common Objects in Context. arXiv:1405.0312v3 [cs.CV] 21 Feb 2015.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Images were collected from Flickr by querying for pairs of object categories or scene/object category pairs to find non-iconic images, downloading at most 5 photos taken by a single photographer within a short time window.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Segmentations were not collected for 11 categories (hat, shoe, eyeglasses, mirror, window, door, street sign, plate, desk, blender, hair brush) due to having too many or too few instances, ambiguity, or confusion with other categories.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Photos uploaded by amateur photographers to Flickr, including searchable metadata and keywords.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Three-stage pipeline using Amazon Mechanical Turk: 1) category labeling using a hierarchical approach, 2) instance spotting by placing a cross on each instance, and 3) instance segmentation using a polygon tool, followed by a verification stage where workers judged segmentation quality.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Category presence was determined if any of the 8 workers indicated it. Segmentations were verified by 3 to 5 workers and discarded if they did not receive at least 4 out of 5 favorable votes.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: 8 for category labeling and instance spotting; 1 for segmentation; 3 to 5 for segmentation verification
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset currently only labels "things" and not "stuff" categories, which may limit contextual information.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: advancing the state-of-the-art in object recognition and scene understanding; detection and segmentation of objects occurring in their natural context
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset was split into two releases (2014 and 2015); the authors state MS COCO will evolve and grow over time, with up to date information available online.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Near-duplicate images were explicitly removed and images were grouped by photographer and date taken to minimize the chance of near-duplicates existing across splits.
